# NOT RUN. What an Astrid agent would hand h3_av.transform (RunPod-only inference) for seq01 C7 "The pouch",
# built from the gate-price-jam references. h3_av references are files (asset map), not reference ids, and
# take still images only (1..9): Snap's voice <Audio n> citation has no home here, and C7 has no line anyway.
version: 1
operation: generate
output: {duration: 3.04}
content:
  prompt: >-
    integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] 2D cel-shaded dark fantasy seinen anime, crisp clean lineart, cold
    desaturated colours, heavy hard shadows, dusk light, falling snow. Close-up insert at hand height: Brann (the old
    headman in <Picture 1>) holds the small leather coin pouch of <Picture 3> in both trembling hands, frame right;
    Maren's (the swordswoman in <Picture 2>) gloved left hand hangs perfectly still at her side, frame left, cut at the
    wrist. The pouch trembles; her hand does not move. Nobody speaks.
    overall_soundscape: leather creaking, coins shifting once inside the pouch (one soft clink), his short nervous breath.
    non_diegetic_music: N/A
changes: {video: [], audio: []}
references:
  - {asset: brann_front.png, purpose: appearance}          # reference "Brann" primary canonical
  - {asset: maren_v4_front.png, purpose: appearance}       # reference "Maren" primary canonical (Snap Cast @7 pictures = v4)
  - {asset: pouch_from_brann_front.png, purpose: appearance}  # reference "The payment pouch" (Astrid-side crop)
overrides: {steps: 6, seed: 12071}                         # Snap's Pika 6-step house rule; h3_av's baseline is 8

# Jam: short03 "The Gate Price" brought into Astrid, then driven as Astrid's agent (2026-11-07 13:13-13:40)

The operator, 2026-11-07: "yeah it can know our plot and stuff and descriptions of scene and characters and stuff and
let's see what it does kinda jam". This was exploration, not production. Everything went into one new project on the lab
Runtime. Nothing in A2's projects, the lab's `src/` or `env/`, Snap, :8193 or GPU1 was changed, and no key, paid call or
remote call was used. One side effect is listed under "Things to know".

## What exists now

| thing | where |
|---|---|
| Astrid project | `gate-price-jam`, id 4b252b145e534fbe8c310037c535b857 (realm-lab, lab Runtime) |
| the v4 cut as an Astrid timeline | 5fc7ac45802b4568af9e6e276cacd649, "The Gate Price v4 (Snap jam)": 6 picture clips on `plate` + 3 dialogue clips on `vo` with their words; 21.79 s |
| App link | http://127.0.0.1:5180/tools/video-editor?project=4b252b145e534fbe8c310037c535b857&timeline=5fc7ac45802b4568af9e6e276cacd649 |
| A/B probe timeline | ca67311e5ed04e9abf8711c4f02f28b3, "probe: plain V1 (jam A/B)", 2 takes on a plain V1 (kept, no deletes) |
| references | 11: Maren, Brann, Liesl, Tam, The hollow (characters); The walled village, The road outside the west gate, The square inside the gate (places); The greatsword, The payment pouch (objects); Maren's harness and scabbard (clothing). 40 media associations (+11 primaries), 13 links |
| documents | 10: snap.story, snap.beats, snap.style, snap.bible, snap.settei-bg, snap.voices, snap.edit, snap.critic, snap.boards (Markdown) + snap.beat-sheet (JSON, a structured beat sheet with per-beat characters, place and story-state) |
| shots + text bindings | 6 project shots "C1 arrival" … "C6 the gate", each holding its take; 15 bindings: `prompt` slot `h3-executed` (the prompt as sent, with `<Picture n>`) and slot `h3-template` (with Snap's `{P:cast:…}` placeholders) on all 6; `transcript` on C2, C3, C5 |
| media | 47 imported via MCP (12 character pictures incl. older Cast versions, 4 masters, 13 plates, 3 plans/maps, 5 voice refs, 7 boards, 3 Astrid-side crops) + 9 from the archive (6 takes, 3 dialogue wavs) + 1 checkout JSON |
| working files | `<study>/jam-gate-price/`: `build_archive.py`, `gate_price_v4_jam.astrid`, `mcp_session.py` (the MCP driver), `cdp_jam.cjs` (one-tab CDP screenshots), `inputs/` (every MCP call list), `mcp/` (every MCP reply, whole), `shots/`, `derived/` (crops, dialogue wavs), `h3_av_request_seq01_C7_NOT_RUN.yaml` |

Screenshots (agents' Chrome, one extra tab, closed after each run):
- `<study>/jam-gate-price/shots/01-timeline.png`
- `<study>/jam-gate-price/shots/02-clip-c2-inspector.png`
- `<study>/jam-gate-price/shots/03-dialogue-brann.png`
- `<study>/jam-gate-price/shots/04-shots-page.png`
- `<study>/jam-gate-price/shots/05-seek-c2.png`
- `<study>/jam-gate-price/shots/06-seek-c6.png`
- render-free filmstrip from Astrid's own `timelines visualize`: `<study>/jam-gate-price/work/materialized/timeline-5fc7ac45802b4568af9e6e276cacd649-png.png`

**Judged as a product.**
- The App shows the cut well: take labels on every clip ("C2 the price · take-032a07b3"), a Dialogue track with
  waveforms, fade markers (IN:FADE / OUT:FADE) and real frames when you seek (05: Brann holding out the pouch at 6.04 s).
- Everything else that came in is invisible in the App:
  - no references view and no documents view;
  - the inspector shows only effects, timing and position, not the prompt, the take's Snap metadata or the line;
  - no words or line text at the playhead, even mid-line;
  - `/shots` says "No shots available for this project", though the Runtime holds 6 shots with 15 text bindings (that
    page is the older image-shot gallery).
- An agent can read everything through MCP; the person can see only the cut.

## Mapping table

| Cast versions (@1-@7) and the picture each carried | none. One reference with many associations | older pictures associated as `depicts` with `metadata.snap.cast_version` / `superseded_by` | **squashed**: no versions, no head, no "what @4 looked like"; `set_primary` overwrites. Version history lives only in metadata |

Non-speaking cuts keep sound inside the video clip |

## What Astrid did with the context

**Good**
- **Words.** With the lines on `vo` clips, `timelines words` listed all 11 words with timeline times and cut ids
  (`agreed...` 5.638-6.318 in c2). `timelines lines` gave the 3 lines with spans. `timelines find "price"` answered
  "heard 'price' · 4.78-5.24 s · in c2 (C2 the price)". `words eyes` says what is on screen and what is anchored there.
  This is the strongest thing Astrid adds over Snap's Cut today.
- **Faithful import.** One atomic commit, 9 media re-hashed, and the labels, fades and `generation.snap` came through
  whole. The App plays the real frames.
- **Render-free filmstrip.** `timelines visualize --view filmstrip --mode inputs` produced a clean declared-inputs sheet
  (png + md) without a render.
- **Agent-shaped answers.** Every refusal said what to do next: pacing named the missing `bundle`, invoke said to import
  the file and pass its digest, the import named the undeclared element. This is much better than a stack trace.
- **Reference handles in edits.** `timelines edit --swap-asset ref:NAME` can point a clip at a reference's media. This is
  the one place an edit consumes references.

**Useless here (or blocked)**
- **Planning.**
  - `editorial.script_pipeline` is the only "write me a shot list" tool. Its only presets are sitcom ones (always_sunny,
    seinfeld), live mode needs a DeepSeek key, and fake mode fails, because its invocation never forwards the inputs.
  - `editorial.arrange` (LLM, needs a pool from the hype pipeline) is built to cut raw footage into hype videos. It
    doesn't plan a narrative.
  - No Astrid tool reads project documents or references as planning context. So it produced **no shot list** to
    compare with `seq01/SEQUENCE.md`. What Astrid could *hold* of SEQUENCE's 16 cuts:
    - the cuts as clips (4 reused takes + placeholders);
    - a `prompt` binding per shot;
    - 3 transcript bindings;
    - a text-card title and fades.
  - What it can't hold: beats with state changes, intensity, marks, camera poses, board model per cut, seed pairs,
    reuse decisions and the transitions' *reasons*.
- **Consistency across references.** The only checker is `understanding.visual_understand`, which needs an OpenAI key.
  `timelines lint` ran locally but only flags 6 × HOLD ("4.46 s with no element event"). For a seinen short of held
  stillness, every one of those is deliberate, and the fix it suggests (mark `deliberate_hold`) needs an edit MCP can't
  make.
- **Titles and transitions.** Astrid has the elements (text-card, fade, cross-fade). But over MCP every non-literal edit
  is refused, and on this imported timeline even a literal trim is refused (see gaps). So no title went in.
- **Generation proposals.** No pack reads references to propose anything. `h3_av.transform` (RunPod-only) takes up to
  9 still images as files and no audio, so Snap's voice citation can't travel. I wrote, but did not run, what an agent
  would hand it for seq01 C7, with the reference pictures mapped by hand:
  `<study>/jam-gate-price/h3_av_request_seq01_C7_NOT_RUN.yaml`.
  `generate_describe h3` shows its inputs: request, asset_map, execution_request, worker_qualification…
  `generate_targets` points at a ComfyUI on 127.0.0.1:8188 (nothing listening). No generation was attempted.

**Surprising**
- References are permissive. A voice wav is accepted as a character's `canonical` media. "The hollow wears Brann"
  (character wears character) is accepted. The symmetric `related_to` mirrored "son of" onto Liesl.
- The App changes the **workspace-wide** current project when you open a timeline (see "Things to know").
- The archive route accepted an Astrid-idiom timeline that Astrid's own editor then can't edit (below).

## Protocol gaps (each also a row in INTEROP_LOG.md tagged "protocol gap")

1. **MCP serves only 6 skills** (astrid, creative-work, pack-builder, pack-testing, editorial, understanding). The
   references, timeline, timeline-shots/narrated, rendering, generation and h3_av skills exist, but `skill_get` says
   "unknown skill". An MCP-only agent can't learn how to use references or shot text.
2. **A binary archive can't go through MCP.** `timelines_import` writes `file` as UTF-8 text ("File is not a zip
   file"). Snap's handoff needs the CLI, or a path/URL/object-id argument.
3. **Elements must be declared.** An archive using a fade must list
   `{"packId":"rendering","kind":"animation","id":"fade","pinned":false}`, else "element inventory does not match".
   Snap can't know Astrid's element catalog: contract v2 should list the built-ins Snap may use.
4. **Shot text has no home on an imported cut.**
   - Bindings need registered shots. A flat parent cut has none.
   - `timelines restructure` only splits a one-placement film ("not a chapter film").
   - So the bindings sit on project shots that aren't the timeline's cuts, and `editorial.pacing` can't read the cut
     ("no placed occurrences").
   - Archive v2 should carry `placements` + `shots` with `text_bindings`, which `prepare_import` already retargets
     (`astrid/sdk/timeline_import_prepare.py` `_retarget_text_bindings`).
5. **MCP can't make working-copy edits.** The server always adds `--json`, and the timeline CLI refuses `--json` for
   anything but literal media add/move/trim: no titles, entrances or `deliberate_hold` from an MCP agent.
6. **References lack the roles Cast needs.** There is no voice/picture distinction, no versions, no states, and no
   directed relations beyond five kinds. Link metadata comes back as a `metadata_json` string, while association
   metadata comes back as an object.
7. **No pack consumes references for generation.** h3_av takes files, stills only, RunPod only, and no audio
   references. generate_image only records reference ids as lineage.
8. **Planning tools don't take project context.** `invoke` inputs are strings/objects, so documents and references
   can't be passed as context. The only script tool is broken and sitcom-shaped.
9. **The App's project selection is workspace-global.** Two agents (or an agent and the person) sharing one Runtime
   overwrite each other's "current project".
10. **Nothing to see in the App.** References, documents, shots and text bindings have no view, so the person can't see
    what the agent handed over.
11. *(from the build)* The archive's Snap metadata is opaque, and nothing on either side checks it. I wrote today's Cast
    heads instead of the takes' pins, and the fix commit was refused. The export must read pins from Snap's take
    records, and Astrid needs one agreed slot for "made from" (`generation.snap` today).

## Ideas for the UX/protocol design pass

1. **A Snap → Astrid "project pack" export.** One `.astrid` file (or a sibling `.astrid-project`) holding:
   - the Cut as `placements + shots`, so text bindings sit on the real cuts;
   - per shot: prompt (executed + template), transcript, speaker;
   - references built from Snap records, never from loose files: Cast with its pinned version, all pictures with view
     names, voice as a typed role, props, location with plates and camera poses;
   - documents: story, the beat sheet with state changes as JSON, style, critic rounds.

   Astrid would need three additions to take it: a reference import in the archive manifest, a `voice` association
   role, and version labels on associations. Until then, Snap can write it in two steps: the archive, then a references
   + documents script over MCP (what this jam did by hand in ~150 MCP calls).
2. **Two-way links.**
   - Each Astrid reference carries `snap: {record_id, version}`, and each clip carries `generation.snap.take`.
   - Snap stores the Astrid project/timeline/reference ids it exported to.
   - A re-export updates in place by those ids (swap the asset, set the binding with `expected_head`, `set_primary` with
     a version label) instead of making a new timeline.
3. **What Astrid should send back.**
   - Proposals, not writes: "re-take C4", "this reference picture disagrees with Cast @7", "hold c1 is deliberate",
     "title at 0.6 s".
   - Each carries the Astrid ids it was based on (the head revision, the binding head) so Snap can mark it stale, like
     G15's proposals.
   - Word times from Astrid's transcript tools are worth sending back as Snap Cut markers.
4. **Make the handoff visible to the person.** Ask Astrid for read-only references, documents and shot-text panels in
   the editor. Until then, Snap should show "exported to Astrid: N references, M documents, K bindings" with the App
   link.
5. **Style as a project preference.** Snap's STYLE S1 is literally prompt text. It belongs in Astrid's project
   preferences (injected into prompts). That needs the person's OK, because MCP deliberately can't write preferences.
6. **One shared voice/dialogue model.** H3 takes are joint AV; Astrid wants VO clips with words. Agree that speaking
   cuts export as picture + "own sound" clip (`audio_for` relation, once U1 is fixed), with speaker + line + words on
   the sound clip.
7. **Per-agent selection.** Ask for the App's current project to be per-session, not workspace-global (gap 9).

## Things to know

- **The App changed A2's current project.** Opening the App on `gate-price-jam` (18:32:55Z) switched the Runtime's
  workspace-wide current project to `gate-price-jam`. Before that it was most likely A2's `gate-price-test`, which A2
  had open in the App at 13:14-13:26. My `astrid projects select gate-price-test` was refused by the permission check,
  so it is still `gate-price-jam`. A2's commands pass `--project` explicitly (the contract does). Anything relying on the
  selection, and A2's App tab on reload, may now show the jam project. To restore it, A2 or the coordinator runs
  `astrid projects select gate-price-test`.
- **The timeline carries wrong Cast pins.** `generation.snap.casts` says Maren@7 / Liesl@4, and the vo clips name the
  v2 voice files. The v4 takes were made with Maren@6, Brann@3 and Liesl@3 (v1 voices, VOICES.md 05:20). The fix commit
  was refused (U6), so the timeline keeps the wrong values. Snap's take records are the source of truth.
- **Leftover tasks.** Three failed tasks (pacing ×2, script_pipeline ×1) and one checkout JSON imported as media
  (sha256:9741b289…) are in the jam project. No pending changes are left (`timelines_pending_list` empty) and the
  working copy was discarded.
- **Time.** ~27 min from project creation (13:16) to the last App screenshot (13:34). Could have been faster: build
  the archive in the plain V1 shape first (editable), add the Astrid idioms one at a time, and bisect U7 then.
